articles.title: Kupwara border villages without fire stations, residents fear delayed emergency response
articles.description: Kupwara, Nov 21: Residents of several remote border areas of north Kashmir's Kupwara district have raised concerns over the absence of fire stations, saying thousands of people remain vulnerable to fire emergencies due to delays in accessing firefighting services. Keran, a remote border area that has emerged as a popular tourist destination in recent years, comprises four panchayats with a population of more than 6,000. Despite its growing tourist footfall, the area has no fire station. Mumtaz Ahmad Khoja, general secretary of the Trade Federation Keran, told Greater Kashmir that heavy snowfall during winter forces residents to rely on traditional bukharis and electric heaters, increasing the risk of accidental fires. "Whenever a fire breaks out in a residential house or any other structure, assistance has to be sought either from the local Army unit or the fire station at Kralpora. It takes a fire tender at least one-and-a-half hours to reach Keran. By then, the affected structure often suffers extensive damage or is completely gutted," he said. Former Block Development Council Chairman Keran Mohammad Syed said several properties worth crores of rupees had been lost to fires over the years. "Despite repeated representations to the concerned department for establishing a fire station in Keran, nothing has been done so far. A fire station at the tehsil headquarters is essential to ensure a prompt response and protect lives and property," he said. In Machil, another remote area along the Line of Control (LoC) with a population of more than 10,000, residents have expressed resentment over the withdrawal of a firefighting facility last year. Former Sarpanch Habibullah said a mini fire tender was stationed in Machil last year but was later shifted to the district headquarters without any explanation to the residents. Residents have urged the local MLA and the Jammu and Kashmir government to restore the facility and establish a full-fledged fire station in the area. People in other far-flung border villages, including Jumagund and Budnamal, have also flagged the absence of fire service facilities, saying the lack of timely assistance puts lives and property at risk during emergencies. The residents have appealed to the Omar Abdullah-led government to prioritise fire stations in these areas, particularly ahead of winter, when the increased use of bukharis and heating appliances raises the risk of residential fires. Meanwhile, Assistant Director, Fire and Emergency Services, Kupwara, Mohammad Arif Mir told Greater Kashmir that a fire station had been established in Machil under the winter preparedness programme but was withdrawn after the season ended. "The fire station is winter-specific as most fire incidents are reported during winters," he said. Mir said a similar fire station was being established in Keran.
